fail_open_ruling.scope: NOT CP3, NOT CP4, NOT a regression. NEW ISSUE (needs the user's authorization to file).
fail_open_ruling.rationale: (1) Pre-existing since issue #33: check_project_locked (project_discovery.py:262-274) has returned None -> 'not locked' -> proceed on dir_result None since long before the CP series; ad1d50c did not introduce it. (2) NO data-loss path: if the projects directory cannot be resolved, the subprocess cannot resolve the project either, so the write fails at LCM open time and lands in CP3's post-hoc _diagnose_project_open_error. LCM remains the backstop; the gate is vacuous, not bypassed. (3) The real fix -- a 6th verdict 'unknown' / blocking:null -- widens an enum consumed by build_access_remedy, build_lock_diagnosis, the CP4 gate, diagnostic_health, ProjectLockedDetail and 30+ tests. Folding an enum widening into the tail of a hardening cycle is precisely the unbounded drift that has already cost two cycles.
fail_open_ruling.recommended_shape_when_filed: Additive `probed: bool = True` on ProjectAccess, set False in the dir-unresolvable branch; a real verdict='unknown' only if a consumer actually needs to branch on it. Recorded here so it is not relitigated from scratch.
fail_open_ruling.interim_patch_ruled_IN_for_cycle_7: ad1d50c NEWLY PUBLISHES `blocking` in the validate_only payload. We own not shipping a brand-new field that asserts false confidently. Cycle 7 must emit blocking:null (and omit the verdict) when the probe did not actually probe. Scope is the reporting sites + the ProjectAccess flag ONLY -- the CP4 gate's dispatch is NOT to be touched.
